criteria.name: layer_separation
criteria.evidence: Positive: PaymentApi.kt:30-66 holds no SQL or bank calls; HttpBankClient.kt:17-59 holds only HTTP; PaymentService.kt:17 orchestrates via repository + port. Negative: application layer imports the HTTP DTO (PaymentService.kt:3, 23) and returns HTTP status codes from the service (PaymentService.kt:28, 51, 68; SettlementService.kt:17, 23, 27). The repository owns state transitions and money movement (PaymentRepository.kt:46-63) and the whole settlement business rule set, including snapshot cutoff, fee aggregation and agency balance increment (PaymentRepository.kt:82-100), so SQL and state transition share one class.

criteria.name: replaceable_bank_port
criteria.evidence: BankPort.kt:12-15 defines the port in the application package with a sealed result type (BankPort.kt:5-10) covering Succeeded/Declined/Unknown/Absent. HttpBankClient.kt:18-22 is the only implementation, in infrastructure, and maps HTTP/exception outcomes to the sealed type (HttpBankClient.kt:46-58). PaymentService.kt:17 depends on the interface only. Minor: the experiment hook `fault` is part of the port signature (BankPort.kt:13).

criteria.name: explicit_state_and_transaction_boundaries
criteria.evidence: Payment creation uses an explicit TransactionTemplate block for insert + reserve (PaymentService.kt:36-47), calls the bank outside any transaction (PaymentService.kt:52), then confirms in a second explicit transaction (PaymentService.kt:60-66). Transitions are guarded by status='PENDING' predicates (PaymentRepository.kt:49, 59, 66) and DB CHECK constraints (V1__payment_business.sql:14, 2). Recovery uses a lease column with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (PaymentRepository.kt:69-74). Settlement is one transaction serialized per agency by a row lock (SettlementService.kt:13-28, PaymentRepository.kt:80). Weakness: status is a raw String (Models.kt:9) compared by literal in six places.

criteria.name: cohesive_money_idempotency_methods
criteria.evidence: Money is cohesive: feeFor uses multiplyExact and integer floor (Models.kt:19), fee rate and fee are persisted per payment (PaymentService.kt:42-43), balance/reserve/ledger moves are single SQL statements with DB invariants (PaymentRepository.kt:41-63, V1__payment_business.sql:2, 28). Idempotency is not cohesive: the same-payload comparison is written twice (PaymentService.kt:26 and 49), the status-to-HTTP-code map three times (PaymentService.kt:28, 51, 68), and the settlement key/payload check twice (SettlementService.kt:14-18 and 20-24). The bank key is derived inline as a string template (PaymentService.kt:42) rather than in a domain function.

criteria.name: error_recovery_tests
criteria.evidence: Present: fee floor and key validation (DomainTest.kt:11-25); 100 same-key concurrent requests, tenant 404, payload 409, float 400 (PaymentIntegrationTest.kt:67-85); overdraw guard (88-104); decline 422 with zero deduction and timeout-after/timeout-before/5xx convergence with one ledger row (107-126); 50 concurrent settlements (129-148); late-confirmation KST snapshot (151-171). Missing despite requirements.md line 45: no restart/SIGKILL test, no DB-outage-between-bank-and-confirm test, no 403 header-mismatch or 404 unknown user/agency test, no persistent-outage behavior test, and no test that drives PaymentService with a fake BankPort. All recovery tests are gated by RUN_INTEGRATION (PaymentIntegrationTest.kt:22) and need a live bank.

criteria.name: limited_duplication_and_abstraction
criteria.evidence: No spurious interfaces: repository and services are concrete, only BankPort is abstracted. Duplication: idempotency check and status map repeated in PaymentService.kt:26/49 and 28/51/68; settlement key check repeated SettlementService.kt:14-18/20-24; agency-mismatch guard repeated PaymentApi.kt:39-40/55-56; key lookup performed twice per create (PaymentService.kt:24 and 37). Services return untyped Pair<Model, Int> (PaymentService.kt:23, SettlementService.kt:13).

findings.cause: Application service depends on the HTTP request DTO and returns HTTP status integers (lines 23, 28, 51, 68).
findings.impact: Layer inversion; the service cannot be reused or unit-tested without the web layer's types, and HTTP semantics are decided in two layers.
findings.remediation: Introduce an application-level command (userId, amount, currency) and a result type such as Created/Replayed/Pending/Failed; map to 201/200/202/422 in PaymentApi.

findings.cause: Same-payload comparison duplicated at lines 26 and 49; status-to-code mapping duplicated at lines 28, 51, 68.
findings.impact: Idempotency semantics can drift between the pre-check and the in-transaction check; a change to one path is easy to miss in the other.
findings.remediation: Add a single samePayload(prior, request) function and a single replayStatus(payment) function, and call them from both paths.

findings.cause: createSettlement contains the settlement business rules: cutoff snapshot, KST date window, item claiming, aggregation, and the agency balance increment.
findings.impact: Business decisions live in the persistence class; the service (SettlementService.kt:26) is a thin pass-through and the rules are not visible or testable outside SQL.
findings.remediation: Keep the statements in the repository but split them into named steps (insertSettlement, claimItems, totalize, creditAgency) invoked in order by SettlementService inside its transaction.

findings.cause: No regression test for restart (C13), DB outage between bank success and confirmation (C14), 403 mismatch, 404 unknown user/agency, or persistent bank outage; no fake BankPort test.
findings.impact: The recovery paths that matter most in the contract are unverified by the submitted suite.
findings.remediation: Add a service-level test with a fake BankPort returning Unknown/Absent/Succeeded sequences, a test that kills and restarts the context with a PENDING row, and a test that fails the confirm transaction and asserts convergence.

findings.cause: If the confirm transaction throws (DB down after bank success), the exception propagates to ApiErrors and becomes 503 without a paymentId.
findings.impact: Contract says fault-induced unknown outcome is 202; the caller receives no identifier for a payment that the bank may already hold. Recovery still converges via the lease.
findings.remediation: Catch DataAccessException around the confirm transaction and return the in-memory PENDING payment with 202.

findings.cause: A declined payment is always rendered as the error body and never as a payment body.
findings.impact: The client never learns the paymentId of a FAILED payment and cannot GET it; replay returns 422 again with no id.
findings.remediation: Include paymentId in the 422 body or return the payment body with status FAILED.

findings.cause: Payment.status is a String; literals PENDING/SUCCEEDED/FAILED appear in PaymentService.kt:28, 51, 68, 82 and repository SQL.
findings.impact: Typos compile; transitions are not enumerable.
findings.remediation: Introduce a PaymentStatus enum and map it in the repository row mapper.

findings.cause: 32 semaphore permits feed an 8-thread executor with an unbounded queue while the claim lease is 10 seconds (PaymentRepository.kt:70).
findings.impact: Under DB or bank slowness a queued task can outlive its lease and a second worker can process the same payment. Guards at PaymentRepository.kt:49/59 keep the effect single, but bank calls may be repeated.
findings.remediation: Set permits equal to worker threads, or re-check processing_until before acting.

findings.cause: Catch-all maps every unexpected exception to 503, including NoResourceFoundException and method-not-allowed.
findings.impact: Unknown paths and wrong methods report as service outage and would count against the unexpected-5xx budget.
findings.remediation: Map framework 4xx exceptions explicitly or extend ResponseEntityExceptionHandler.

findings.cause: Migration alters the fixture-owned users table (adds reserved_minor and a CHECK).
findings.impact: If the evaluator resets by reloading users from fixture, the column disappears while Flyway history says V1 is applied. The CHECK also scans 1,000,000 rows at migrate time.
findings.remediation: Keep reservations in an implementer-owned table keyed by user_id, or document the dependency for the evaluator.

findings.cause: Experiment fault hook is part of the port contract.
findings.impact: Any replacement adapter must accept a parameter that has no meaning outside the experiment.
findings.remediation: Pass the fault via a separate experiment-only decorator or a request-scoped context.

unverified_runtime_requirements: Bank adapter semantics depend on infra/README.md, which is not in the packet: GET 404 is treated as 'absent, safe to resend' (HttpBankClient.kt:54) and any 200 whose status is not SUCCEEDED is treated as unknown and retried forever (HttpBankClient.kt:49-53).
30-second convergence after fault release for timeout-before, timeout-after, 5xx, restart, and DB outage (C11-C14).
Effect-once guarantees under C06/C07/C16 concurrency; the SQL guards look correct but were not executed here.
Load SLOs, pool saturation behaviour, RSS growth during soak, and dropped_iterations (C20).
Behaviour of the users-table alteration and CHECK constraint on the 1,000,000-row fixture during evaluator resets.
The integration suite only runs with RUN_INTEGRATION=true against a live bank and fixture DB; the Dockerfile's build-time test run therefore executes DomainTest only.
